label.trigger: RAND_write_file is called on a path that already names a regular file, and opening it and filling the 256-byte buffer both succeed. The buffer goes to the stdio stream as a single element of 256 bytes, so a complete write makes the stream call report 1, and that element count is then tested against 256.
label.expected_impact: Every save that actually succeeds is reported as a failure: the seed file on disk receives all 256 bytes, yet the function closes the stream and hands back -1 instead of the byte count. A caller that trusts the result treats a good seed file as unwritten, and because the early exit skips OPENSSL_cleanse, the random bytes are left in the stack buffer.

anchors.start: if (fwrite(buff, sizeof buff, 1, out) != sizeof buff) {

context_locations.note: The buffer is 256 bytes long, so the value the stream result is measured against is 256, while a call that asks for one element can only ever yield 0 or 1.
The intended success exit wipes the buffer and returns the byte length; with the faulty test no write can reach it.

known_counterevidence.note: The bytes do reach the file before the false failure, so a caller that ignores the result or only checks that the file exists sees nothing amiss. No code inside the analysed directory calls the function; the effect shows only through the public interface.

label.fix_summary: Test the stream write result against the one element that was requested instead of against the buffer length in bytes.
distinctive_tokens: treats a good seed file as unwritten

check.summary: Builds the unchanged randfile.c against two minimal stand-in headers and a driver that supplies the random source, the cleanse routine and the string copy. The driver creates an empty regular file in the check home, asks the library to save a seed into it, and requires the reported result to equal the size found on disk afterwards.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with gcc 15.2.0 (-fsanitize=address,undefined): on before the driver prints that the save reported -1 while the file holds 256 bytes and exits 1; on after it reports 256 for 256 bytes and exits 0. The project's generated public headers are not built: two minimal stand-in headers and driver-defined stand-ins for the random source, the cleanse routine and the string copy replace them, and randfile.c itself is compiled unchanged. The fix was merged 2026-03-10 (first-tier recency rule). needs_cross_file is false: the defect and its evidence sit in one file of the scope; the return contract is also stated in the manual page outside the scope (doc/man3/RAND_load_file.pod), which is not labelled.
